label: rem:breit-wheeler-observation
title: Breit--Wheeler process: observation and comparison with the model selection rule
html:
The Breit--Wheeler polarisation selection rule (13.12.3) is a model statement: in the model, only distinct generators (\sigma_0 \neq \sigma_1) contribute to pair production. This block records what the rule implies and how it compares with measurement.

Model consequences

For two photons with polarisation mixing parameters \phi_1,\phi_2\in[0,1], the Hecke normal form yields the same-mode amplitude S = \phi_1\phi_2 + (1-\phi_1)(1-\phi_2) and the pair-production amplitude C_+ + C_- = 1 - S. The pair-production threshold energy scale is

  E_0(\phi_1,\phi_2)
  = 
  \frac{2m_e}{\mathrm{net}(e^+) - S \cdot h_{\mathrm{A}}}
   \in [2.27,4.22] \text{MeV},

where h_{\mathrm{A}} = q - q^{-1} \approx 0.209 at q_0 and \mathrm{net}(e^+) \approx 0.451 (the Gröbner--Shirshov NF coefficient at q_0).

Evaluate the limits:

Configuration S E_0 Character
Same mode (\phi_1 = \phi_2) 1 \approx 4.22 \mathrm{MeV} Hecke-reduced; no pair in the model
Distinct modes (\phi_1 \neq \phi_2) 0 \approx 2.27 \mathrm{MeV} L_\pm; pair

For unpolarised beams, the cross-section averages over \phi_1,\phi_2 and develops a \cos(2\phi) azimuthal modulation in the e^-e^+ opening-angle distribution. The amplitude is proportional to \langle C_+ - C_- \rangle = \langle \phi_1 - \phi_2 \rangle^2.

Comparison with observation

Ultra-peripheral heavy-ion collisions provide colliding quasi-real photons that are linearly polarised transverse to the beam axis. STAR [star2021bw] reports a fourth-order azimuthal modulation \cos 4\Delta\phi = (16.8 \pm 2.5)\% of e^-e^+ pairs in Au+Au collisions at \sqrt{s_{NN}} = 200\,\mathrm{GeV}, where \Delta\phi is the angle between the pair transverse momentum and that of one lepton. Lowest-order QED predicts 16.5\%. ATLAS [atlas2021bw] reports the azimuthal anisotropy of e^-e^+ pairs in Pb+Pb collisions at \sqrt{s_{NN}} = 5.02\,\mathrm{TeV}.

These measurements do not support the model's selection rule. The measured effect is a fourth harmonic that lowest-order QED reproduces, while the model's averaged amplitude above is a second harmonic. QED also gives nonzero pair production for parallel linear polarisations (13.12.3), so the model's suppression of same-mode pairs is not a property of physical photons. No agreement with data is claimed here.

The model's distinct-mode scale E_0 \approx 2.27\,\mathrm{MeV} does not decompose as 2m_e plus one unit of Reeb charge: \hbar_q = (q-1)/q \approx 0.0991 is dimensionless, and m_e\hbar_q \approx 0.0506\,\mathrm{MeV}, not 1.25\,\mathrm{MeV}.
